label: Disability
assignment: Discover realistic disability resources for people in {service_area}, including benefits, independent living, assistive technology, home- and community-based support, advocacy, employment, transportation, and caregiver help. Follow broad agencies to specific programs while verifying disability criteria, age, funding, waitlists, service area, and the real application or assessment path.
include: Disability benefits, Medicaid pathways, waivers, and benefits counseling
Independent-living skills, personal assistance, home modifications, and community support
Assistive technology, durable equipment, communication access, and device lending
Advocacy, legal rights, education, employment, transportation, recreation, and peer support
Caregiver training, respite, navigation, and services across childhood-to-adult transitions
exclude: General services that merely claim accessibility without a disability-specific benefit or accommodation
Equipment sellers without a subsidy, loan, reuse, assessment, or hardship-access program
Programs whose diagnostic, age, waiver, or geographic limits make local access unrealistic
verificationQuestions: Which disabilities, functional needs, ages, or benefit statuses qualify?
Is diagnosis or professional referral required, and who performs assessments?
What funding source, cost share, waitlist, and service limit applies?
Are communication, physical, sensory, cognitive, and language accommodations actually available?

stages.title: Benefits and navigation
stages.instruction: Investigate SSI and SSDI help, Medicaid and waiver pathways, benefits counseling, disability determination support, case navigation, and the actual application, appeal, or assessment process.

stages.title: Independent living and equipment
stages.instruction: Investigate personal assistance, independent-living skills, home modifications, assistive technology, durable equipment, communication access, device lending, repair, reuse, and funding.

stages.title: Participation and caregiver support
stages.instruction: Investigate advocacy, education transitions, employment, transportation, recreation, peer support, respite, caregiver help, and services responsive to intellectual, developmental, physical, sensory, and psychiatric disabilities.

stages.title: Waitlists and access gap review
stages.instruction: Cross-check diagnostic and functional criteria, age transitions, waiver status, waitlists, rural reach, accommodations, and costs. Identify services described as accessible that lack a practical access path.
